For oscillatory Gaussian perturbations, this overlap is the coherent sum of the positive- and negative-frequency branches of the source, with its amplitude factorizing exactly into a Gaussian spectral envelope and an interference factor. We observe that the excitation amplitude peaks at $
u=\omega_n^{m Re}$ only for narrowband sources. For sufficiently broadband pulses, the maximum lies at $
u=0$, so efficient excitation does not necessarily require matching the carrier and the mode frequency. We observe that the interference between branches, modulates the amplitude only for nonzero $
u$, a feature generic to real oscillatory sources. The prominence of the interference-induced modulation is controlled by the ratio $\omega_n^{m Re}/\omega_n^{m Im}$. The phase separates into a mode-only, a width-only and a $
u$-dependent term, the last generated by the same interference, with $
u=0$ being its unique maximum at fixed width. The analytical predictions are validated against time-domain numerical simulations, showing a relative median error of $\sim 4\%$ for $|C_0|$. For $|C_1|$, the median error is $\sim 16\%$ when $\sigma\leq 5$, increasing to $\sim 36\%$ across the full parameter space. The median phase difference for $n=0$ is $\sim0.14 \,m rad $ and for $n=1$, $\sigma\leq5$ it is $0.34\,m rad$. Our results demonstrate that QNM excitation cannot be understood through frequency matching alone and may provide qualitative insights into more realistic astrophysical scenarios.
papers.authors: Alejandro Svyatkovskyy Kholyavka, Sayak Datta, Jose Antonio Le\'on Vega, Xisco Jim\'enez Forteza

papers.title: Four-charge Rotating AdS Black Holes in Gauged STU Supergravity
papers.abstract: We present an exact solutions for non-extremal rotating AdS black holes with four independent charges in four-dimensional gauged STU supergravity. The scalar potential introduced by gauging breaks the hidden symmetry underlying solution-generating methods in the ungauged theory, making the construction of such solutions a longstanding challenge. We analyse the global properties of the solution and derive its thermodynamic quantities. We further take the BPS limit and show that the resulting entropy agrees with the known microscopic result obtained from the dual conformal field theory.
papers.authors: Liang Ma, H. Lu

papers.title: Tripartite nonlocal magic from reflected and negativity spectra
papers.abstract: A tripartite pure state is local-unitary equivalent to a stabilizer state if and only if its marginal, reflected, and negativity spectra (up to signs) are flat. These conditions are quantified using anti-flatness, giving a diagnostic of tripartite nonlocal magic that is computable and experimentally measurable using randomized measurements. In non-abelian quantum doubles, it appears only when the triple points of the tripartition lie on plaquettes. In random tensor networks, it appears exactly when the entanglement wedge of two boundary regions connects.
papers.authors: Sriram Akella

papers.title: The Supercritical Ten Martini Problem
papers.abstract: We solve the ten martini problem for the positive-Lyapunov part of the spectrum of any nonconstant real analytic one-frequency Schr\"odinger operator. The proof uses the intrinsic symplectic structure of the dual center of Ge--Jitomirskaya [28] and extends the Kotani--almost-reducibility strategy of Ge--Jitomirskaya--You [30] from two-dimensional centers to arbitrary finite center dimension.
papers.authors: Lingrui Ge, Svetlana Jitomirskaya, Jiangong You

papers.title: Universal Fold Caustics in Anharmonic Matter-wave Lenses
papers.abstract: Caustics provide a universal connection between classical ray focusing and structured wave patterns. We theoretically investigate this connection in non-linear matter waves focused by a short-duration anharmonic lens acting on a Bose-Einstein condensate. A semi-classical description shows how the leading cubic aberration transforms the harmonic focal point into a fold caustic, whose local wave field is described by an Airy canonical integral. Three-dimensional Gross-Pitaevskii simulations show that mean-field interactions modify the near-focus density and longitudinal momentum distribution, producing a secondary momentum-space feature absent from the non-interacting evolution. We quantify the information about the effective interaction strength carried by the $1D$ distribution using classical Fisher information and maximum-likelihood estimation. We obtain a relative uncertainty of $2.7\times10^{-3}$ for a sample of $10^5$ detected points along $z$. These results establish a framework for studying interaction-driven departures from single-particle caustic universality and promote matter-wave lenses as a sensitive probe of mean-field interactions.
papers.authors: Joachim Guyomard, Julia Pahl, Ernst Rasel, Naceur Gaaloul

papers.title: Second-level termination of the PPT entanglement-cost hierarchy for two qutrits
papers.abstract: We prove that for arbitrary two-qutrit quantum states, the semidefinite programming lower-bound hierarchy for the PPT entanglement cost terminates at the second level. Therefore, under operations preserving positive partial transpose, its zero-error asymptotic entanglement cost can be obtained by a semidefinite program involving only three Hermitian matrix variables. The key to the proof is to shorten the feasible dual chain by one level; to this end, we combine finite certificates verified by exact rational arithmetic with analytic estimates near the boundary of the parameter domain. This result shows that a unified terminating level exists for two-qutrit systems, whereas no unified terminating level exists for all dimensions.
papers.authors: Wei Song, Xiao-Lan Zong, Ming Yang

papers.title: Parametric Proof-Carrying Compilation for Quantum Error-Correction
papers.abstract: We present PC-QEC, a proof-carrying compilation framework for quantum error correction parameterized by both code distance and syndrome-extraction scheme. It covers all four schemes---Standard, Flag, Shor and Knill---with circuit-level distance guarantees for every legal code distance in each proved family under the declared fault and readout contracts. The circuit-level model permits single-wire Pauli faults at every operation's qubit operands, capturing data errors, readout errors and ancilla faults that propagate into multi-qubit hook errors. For each family and scheme, code-algebra proofs and fault-aware Hoare proofs compose into a finite symbolic certificate whose size is independent of code distance. We demonstrate family-wide guarantees for five code families across all four schemes. For rotated Surface code, one Standard Scheme certificate proves a distance lower bound $d$ for every odd $d\ge3$ and checks in 214\,s on average. Lean 4 mechanizes the metatheory and exact circuit-level distances for canonical Surface, hypergraph-product (HGP) and Toric code families.
papers.authors: John Zhuoyang Ye, Jens Palsberg

papers.title: Time Running Backwards, and Where It Stops: Superoscillations of Proper Time and the Memory of the Environment
papers.abstract: A quantum system prepared in a superposition of proper times - a clock whose worldline is superposed, or a clock at rest in a superposed gravitational potential - evolves, in each branch, by the same dynamics for a different duration. Post-selecting the control that sets the proper time turns the superposition into a superoscillation of the time-dilation factor: the system is found to have evolved for a proper time $\alpha_w t$, where the weak value $\alpha_w$ may exceed unity, vanish, or be negative - the quantum time-translation machine of Aharonov, Anandan, Popescu and Vaidman. We ask how far back such a machine can run an irreversible process. The test system is a sealed cell - excited atoms, the radiation field they emit into, and the absorbing walls, carried as one quantum object - and the witness is projective: atoms that had begun to decay before the run are found, in the post-selected sub-ensemble, more excited than when inserted. The answer is exact and depends only on the atoms' survival amplitude. With two branches the witness holds only while the decay is younger than the memory time of the environment, after which the emission becomes Markovian. Beyond it, the post-selection amplifies the minute difference between the contents of the cell in the two branches, set by the full energy spread of the atoms and their field rather than by the linewidth, and the witness fails. Reversing a decay past the memory time requires many branches, an environment with a strictly bounded spectrum, and a post-selection probability that falls exponentially with the number of environmental oscillations to be undone. The obstacle to reversal is therefore not entropy but bandwidth - the same bandwidth that makes the emission irreversible in the first place. We give four ways to superpose a clock rate, from hollow massive shells to inertial velocities.
papers.authors: Yakir Aharonov, Avshalom C. Elitzur

papers.title: A constrained mixed variational formulation with Legendre-dual defects for incremental irreversible thermodynamics
papers.abstract: We present a constrained mixed variational formulation for incremental irreversible thermodynamics. A single augmented action combines a linearized contact-increment penalty, equilibrium and dissipative Fenchel--Young defects, a storage--transport functional, and multipliers enforcing the constitutive increments. Under frozen-coefficient and boundary assumptions, stationarity yields the linearized contact condition, the Tisza relation, the Onsager flux--force law, and the implicit balance equation. An exact-elimination theorem shows that the contact and multiplier fields can be reconstructed algebraically from a solution of the reduced weak balance problem. We also prove off-shell invariance of the equilibrium--storage--multiplier sector under an equilibrium-sector partial Legendre transformation; invariance of the full augmented action is not claimed. For Fourier heat conduction, we derive a weighted drift identity and a per-step energy-drift bound for the energy-representation three-term incremental functional. In one spatial dimension, a small-time-step estimate yields a uniform $H^1$ bound and a discrete $L^2(0,T_f;H^2)$ bound, leading to cumulative $O(\delta t)$ drift over fixed time intervals. A conservative mixed discontinuous Galerkin (DG0)--Raviart--Thomas (RT0) discretization with fully implicit conductivity $\kappa(T)=1+T^2$ preserves discrete energy to roundoff. A separate lumped-mass piecewise-linear benchmark reproduces the predicted finite-step drift.
papers.authors: Mostafa Rostampour

papers.title: A Beltrami Mode in Extreme Fractional Hydrodynamics under Stochastic Forcing
papers.abstract: We construct an exact stochastic solution of the extreme order endpoint of adaptive fractional Navier Stokes (AFNS) hydrodynamics on the three-dimensional periodic torus. A helical Beltrami eigenfield reduces the nonlinear vector equation to a scalar Ornstein Uhlenbeck process when the white-in-time forcing is aligned with that eigenfield. The resulting invariant Gaussian law yields explicit formulas for the stationary energy, its fluctuations, temporal correlations, circulation, and helicity. Under the same forcing, the corresponding classical Navier Stokes mode has a stationary energy that diverges as the Reynolds number tends to infinity, while the Euler limit exhibits linear growth of the mean energy and has no invariant probability law. The construction isolates, without a cascade hypothesis, the statistical effect of the finite fractional dissipation retained at the extreme endpoint of AFNS.
papers.authors: Jos\'e I. H. L\'opez

papers.title: First results from a borehole network for the seismic characterization of the Einstein Telescope Euregio Meuse-Rhine candidate site
papers.abstract: The low-frequency sensitivity of the Einstein Telescope depends on the seismic environment of its site, both through the mechanical coupling of ground motion to the test masses and through Newtonian noise. We present the first results of the seismic characterization of the Euregio Meuse-Rhine candidate site based on a network of recently instrumented boreholes covering the first seven months of 2026 at four underground stations and their co-located surface sensors. Two of these boreholes were deliberately sited next to railway infrastructure, so that the levels reported here describe how anthropogenic transients propagate to depth at different distances from the source. The analysis was carried out with \texttt{SiteChar}, a Python framework developed for this work to provide a common processing pipeline across different sensors, networks and observation periods. It processes the data in sequential chunks and separates the noise floor from the contribution of transients. We present a characterization of the catalogue of observed transients and a tentative classification. These measurements form part of an integrated site characterization approach that combines the observed seismic field with three-dimensional geological and wave-propagation models to predict Newtonian noise and ultimately guide its mitigation at the Euregio Meuse-Rhine candidate site.
papers.authors: L. D'Onofrio, S. Koley, P. Barneo, S. Bentvelsen, S. Danilishin, G. Degrande, S. Francois, S. Kadmiel, M. Kiehn, H. Michel, F. Nguyen, T. Niggemann, N. Nippe, J. Pretz, V. Tempel, B. Vink, W. Walk

papers.title: Quantum Simulation of Quantum Channels and Applications
papers.abstract: We review the basic theory of quantum channels and develop a strategy for simulating them on digital quantum computers, drawing upon the Choi-Kraus operator-sum representation and Stinespring dilation to provide a unified approach for various applications. We discuss three types of applications, offering explicit examples for each: the preparation of mixed states, measurements described by positive operator-valued measures (POVMs), and the simulation of the evolution of Markovian quantum systems. We recover fundamental concepts from quantum theory, such as the purification of a mixed state and the Naimark dilation associated with a POVM. Regarding the simulation of the evolution of a Markovian quantum system, we introduce an operator, termed the residual operator, to construct, from the system's Liouvillian, a quantum channel that serves as a first-order approximation of the quantum dynamical semigroup. This allows the simulation of quantum dynamics to be performed in a manner analogous to the Euler method for ordinary differential equations, avoiding Trotterization. We prove all the theoretical results mentioned, with the exception of the fundamental Choi-Kraus theorem concerning the operator-sum representation of quantum channels, for which we provide the appropriate references. The explicit simulations discussed were implemented using the AerSimulator from IBM's Qiskit SDK, with the corresponding code available on GitHub.
papers.authors: L\'{u}cio S. Fassarella

papers.title: Testing non-classical gravitational phase dynamics under strong dephasing
papers.abstract: Whether gravity must be quantum is often approached by asking whether two masses can become entangled through their mutual gravitational interaction. In practice, the weak interaction competes with environmental decoherence, so the final state may contain no entanglement even when the underlying gravitational phase remains coherent. We investigate what can still be learned from the dynamics in a dephased Bose--Marletto--Vedral setup. The dominant Newtonian effect for well-separated paths is an accumulated phase rather than transfer between interferometer arms, a regime motivated by matter-wave gravitational phase experiments and quantified here by wavepacket-overlap and deflection estimates. Keeping independently characterized local which-path dephasing fixed, we prove an exact finite-time distinction between the gravitational conditional-phase evolution and every passive stochastic local-phase model (induced by a classical mediator), including regimes where the chosen input remains separable at all times. The distinction survives, with a modified sensitivity, when the comparison is enlarged to population-preserving classical measurement and feedback through a diagonal PPT relaxation. These results identify an operational test of gravitational phase dynamics in the strong-dephasing regimes, conditional on explicit and physically motivated classical mediator models.
papers.authors: Tianfeng Feng, Vlatko Vedral

papers.title: Imaging spin entanglement with a scanning tunneling microscope
papers.abstract: Artificial spin arrays assembled on surfaces enable atomic-scale studies of quantum correlations. Here we establish a hierarchy of connections between spin inelastic electron tunneling spectroscopy (IETS) and entanglement in spin-$1/2$ systems. We first show that the number of spectroscopically active transitions in a spin-$1/2$ dimer serves as an entanglement witness. Using the leading-order tunneling conductance for the tip placed on spin $i$, $dI(i)/dV$, we then relate spectral moments $\mathcal{M}^{(n)}(i)=\int V^n(d^2I(i)/dV^2)\,dV$ to quantum correlations. The zeroth moment probes the one-tangle in systems with a gapped, nondegenerate ground state. For rotationally invariant Heisenberg systems, the first moment yields thermal spin correlators $\langle\boldsymbol S(i)\cdot\boldsymbol S(j)\rangle$, enabling reconstruction of nearest-neighbor concurrence and spatial imaging of entanglement in spin chains. It also provides access to the internal energy and magnetic specific heat, both usable as entanglement witnesses. Applying this approach to experimental IETS data from nanographene spin chains, we find good agreement with theory. We further discuss how the second moment probes longer-range correlations and the inverse moment relates to local spin susceptibility. For spin-$1/2$ trimers, we connect inter-multiplet inelastic spectral weight to genuine tripartite entanglement quantified by the concurrence fill. Finally, we reconcile the local character of IETS with its sensitivity to nonlocal entanglement through an analogy with digital quantum circuits, where Hamiltonian evolution implements multiqubit operations. These results establish IETS as a tool for quantifying and imaging entanglement in engineered on-surface spin systems.
papers.authors: J. C. G. Henriques, B. Vi\~na-Baus\'a, I. Brihuega, J. Fern\'andez-Rossier

papers.title: Hidden Coherence and Controlled Quasihole Motion in a Fermionic Laughlin State on a Superconducting Quantum Processor
papers.abstract: Fractional quantum Hall (FQH) states support fractionalized excitations and geometric phases, yet experimentally resolving the many-body coherence encoded in their wave functions remains challenging. Here, we prepare a three-electron $\nu=1/3$ Laughlin state on the Haldane sphere using seven superconducting qubits and reconstruct its many-body density matrix. Through Read's composite-boson construction, we reveal vortex-dressed coherence that remains appreciable over a larger separation range than electron coherence. The extended profile is suppressed in a Fock-diagonal reference constructed from the measured populations, demonstrating its dependence on off-diagonal many-body coherence. We further prepare a one-flux-added quasihole and characterize its fractional charge response against finite-size benchmarks. Controlled quasihole motion yields an effective geometric-phase signature from the reconstructed dominant-eigenstate trajectory. These complementary measurements provide microscopic access to the coherent structure and quasihole response of a finite fermionic Laughlin state, demonstrating an experimental route to probing strongly correlated FQH wave functions on programmable quantum processors.
papers.authors: Kui Zhao, Hao Wu, Lei-Yi-Nan Liu, Gui-Han Liang, Cheng-Lin Deng, Cai-Ping Fang, Hao-Tian Liu, Wei-Ping Yuan, Qingyuan Wu, Ziting Wang, Wei-Guo Ma, Hao Li, Jia-Chi Zhang, Tian-Ming Li, Jia-Cheng Song, Zhen-Ting Bao, Zheng-He Liu, Yang He, Yong-Xi Xiao, Yu Liu, Zhongcheng Xiang, Dongning Zheng, Guangming Xue, Haifeng Yu, Kai Xu, Zhao Liu, Kaixuan Huang, Jian Cui, Heng Fan

papers.title: Beyond the Mean Gap: What Transferred-Angle QAOA Retains on a Superconducting Processor
papers.abstract: Hardware executions of the quantum approximate optimization algorithm (QAOA) are often validated by comparing the device's mean cost with a simulation, a check that can miss what matters for optimization. Under global depolarization, the mean normalized gap and the floor-corrected probability of every set of bitstrings, the optimum included, retain the same fraction of their noiseless improvement over uniform sampling. We test this prediction with depth-2, transferred-angle QAOA circuits for binary subproblems of an alternating-direction decomposition on the IBM Heron processor \texttt{ibm\_marrakesh}, with and without dynamical decoupling and twirling. At 12 qubits, the main-family circuits retained 29\% to 46\% of their mean-gap improvement but only 5\% to 15\% of their probability of the optimum, lower on at least nine of ten instances per run. Near-optimal bitstrings were lost about as much as the optimum, whereas the avoidance of poor bitstrings was retained best. In the first submission, a device-matched noise model reproduced the pattern but overestimated the retention of the optimum five- to eightfold. On a rugged planted family, the device found the optimum in 62\% of 768-shot blocks (noiseless: 98\%), within the range of local heuristics. Validations of optimization circuits should report retention of the optimum and of near-optimal sets.
papers.authors: Sanim Yousuf Fahim, Mohammad Arif Hossain

papers.title: Intensity limits for phase-only holographic optical-tweezer arrays
papers.abstract: Optical tweezers use tightly focused laser beams to trap and manipulate individual particles, enabling advances in quantum computing, drug discovery, and biological research. Scaling these technologies to large arrays requires delivering sufficient light to every trapping site while minimizing the total laser power required. Here, we investigate the fundamental limits of how efficiently a phase-only hologram can distribute light across an array of optical traps. We derive upper bounds on the minimum intensity across trapping sites, accounting for illumination, target geometry, and diffraction from spatial light modulator pixels. For arrays arranged in a single plane or across two axial planes, we show how these limits scale with the number of traps and SLM pixels, and establish conditions for focusing light in three dimensions. Numerical experiments demonstrate that optimized holograms can closely approach these theoretical limits, suggesting that further improvements in phase optimization alone offer limited power savings. Instead, our results reveal how the choice of illumination and trap geometry can improve light efficiency, providing practical guidelines for designing larger, more power-efficient optical-tweezer arrays.
papers.authors: Anzhou Wen, Hengyu Lian, Kevin Yipu Wu, Maxwell F. Parsons, Praneeth Chakravarthula

papers.title: Raman anyon-Hubbard model in a 1D Bose lattice gas
papers.abstract: The anyon-Hubbard model is the paradigmatic lattice model of one-dimensional (1D) anyons, in which chiral interactions make bosons equivalent to particles with fractional statistics. Its continuum limit, the chiral BF theory, emerges as the low-energy description of a Raman-coupled Bose gas with imbalanced interactions. Here, we show that loading such a gas into a 1D optical lattice realizes the lattice counterpart of this theory, which we name the Raman anyon-Hubbard model. The Raman-dressed bosons acquire density-dependent Peierls phases when tunneling through occupied sites. For a small statistical phase, the model reduces to the anyon-Hubbard model, while beyond this limit it defines a distinct lattice anyon model with unbounded rather than periodic statistical interactions. Numerically, we show that the dressed gas displays the defining properties of 1D anyons, namely a density-dependent asymmetry of the ground-state momentum distribution, interaction-induced asymmetric transport and chiral bound states. Remarkably, these features are readily accessible with Raman-coupled $^{39}$K atoms, opening up the experimental exploration of 1D anyons beyond the few-particle regime.
papers.authors: Josep Cabedo, Claudio Iacovelli, Leticia Tarruell, Alessio Celi

papers.title: Random encoders and expurgation improve 1,873 entries of the Grassl qubit code tables
papers.abstract: I report 192 explicit binary stabilizer codes $[[n,k,d]]$ with $53\le n\le 254$ and $5\le d\le 13$ whose minimum distance exceeds the lower bound listed in Grassl's code tables at the same $(n,k)$: 161 codes by one and 31 by two. Through the standard propagation rules they raise 1,873 entries of the table. For 190 of the codes, a random Clifford encoder is followed by expurgation: every logical operator of weight below the target distance is enumerated, and a few logical operators are promoted to stabilizers so that each low-weight one anticommutes with at least one of them. The other two are obtained by puncturing a code from the table and repairing it in the same way. All 192 distances are exact: the lower bound is certified by exhaustive meet-in-the-middle enumeration of up to $4\times10^{13}$ Pauli operators, and the upper bound by an explicit logical operator of weight $d$. A first-moment count explains the results. Expurgated random codes have about eight more logical qubits than a typical random code of the same length and distance, so they beat the table wherever its best known codes are no better than random. The largest gains, up to nine logical qubits, are at $d\ge9$ and $n\gtrsim170$, where the table often gives a lower bound without an explicit code. The same count predicts improvements at 619 further pairs $(n,d)$. The search was run by AI agents. The codes, their certificates and an independent checker are public.
papers.authors: Marin Girard

papers.title: Optimal finite-copy readout of three-qubit entanglement with state retention
papers.abstract: For unknown three-qubit pure states, we characterize the optimal trade-off among GHZ-class certification, binary probability readout of the three-tangle, and conditional state retention. The vanishing ideal of the null class specifies the optimal certification subspace, while a polynomial multiplication operator gives the spectral limit for binary readout. Four copies are necessary for a nonzero certificate. A fifth copy raises the optimal success probability from $\tau^{2}/48$ to $5\tau^{2}/72$ and permits the original unknown state to be retained, where $\tau$ is the three-tangle. We obtain this gain as an instance of a general symmetry-based additional-copy theorem. At six copies the optimal certification probability is $(39+2S)\tau^{2}/296$, with $S=\sum_{X}\mathrm{Tr}\,\rho_{X}^{2}$, whereas the largest exact binary probability is $\tau^{2}/8$. Local Schur measurements and conditional local operations with classical communication attain these bounds. Retaining the full six-copy branch record yields a weighted estimator with lower variance than binary thinning of the same data. Explicit circuits and fixed-budget comparisons connect the success probabilities to input-copy consumption, retained quantum output, and coherent gate cost.
papers.authors: Yu-Xin Wu, Yuan-Hong Tao, Ji-Hui Mo, Peng-Fei Ma, Shu-Hui Wu, Shao-Ming Fei

papers.title: Viable Phantom Crossing in Softly Broken Shift Symmetric Gravity
papers.abstract: We demonstrate a viable fit to current cosmological data from a simple Horndeski modified gravity theory that softly breaks shift symmetry. This SBSS model crosses the phantom divide $w=-1$ at $z\approx0.5$ and fits observational data (baryon acoustic oscillations and supernova distances, and cosmic microwave background power spectra) better than $w_0w_a$CDM, by $\Delta\chi^2\approx-3$ for the same number of effective parameters, while providing a physical foundation for cosmic acceleration. The theory is healthy, has no cosmological constant or potential, and has substantial protection against high energy quantum loop corrections.
papers.authors: Rodrigo Calderon, Eric V. Linder

papers.title: Vertex Operator Algebras in Lean: a formal library and its companion book
papers.abstract: We present LeanVOA, a Lean 4 library for the theory of vertex operator algebras (VOAs), together with a companion book that sets each formalized result next to its textbook statement. The library constructs the Moonshine module $V^\natural$ and formalizes Zhu's modular invariance, Huang's tensor categories with the Verlinde formula, the Gannon-Rayhaun classification of $c=1$ VOAs, and classical freeness of the boundary admissible $L_k(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$ (Arakawa-Dai) and of the minimal models $M(2,2m+3)$ (van Ekeren-Heluani). It also contains new results: graded first-order rigidity of all Virasoro minimal models and of $L_k(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$ at every admissible level; classical freeness of $L_{-3/2}(\mathfrak{sl}_3)$, and of the other members of the Deligne series under stated assumptions; and a proof that graded unitarity of the boundary admissible $L_k(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$ implies that of the minimal models $M(2,2n+1)$. The library declares no axiom of its own.
papers.authors: Fedor K. Popov, Leonardo Rastelli

papers.title: Reading Why: Born-Measured Attention with Exact Word Evidence on Light and Qubits
papers.abstract: When a language model answers, we can usually only estimate why. We build a transformer in which every nonlinearity is a quadratic detection (an interference, a balanced interferometric reading or a camera) and the output is a Born probability: attention $|\langle q|k\rangle|^2$, the form of the Born rule, normalised over each row, a measured product in place of the feed-forward nonlinearity, and a Born readout; between detections a classical controller squares, divides, rescales and re-encodes. With its denominators held at their values for the input, each class probability is a polynomial in the word amplitudes, so its integrated-gradient evidence is computed by a finite quadrature with no quadrature error: the words' contributions sum to the class probability above its no-information share, to $10^{-13}$ or better. On e-SNLI natural language inference the model reaches 77.45 +- 0.91 % test accuracy, level within the spread of three seeds with a softmax transformer of the same size (76.62 +- 0.36 %). Deleting the word its evidence ranks first changes the answer in 44 % of test pairs, out of the 53 % any single deletion can change, against 32 % for the softmax model's integrated gradients and 31 % for the Born Transformer's own attention. The same weights compile exactly to optoelectronic optics (simulated), and its attention overlaps to Hadamard tests on qubits; a separate coherent attention layer becomes one post-selected circuit (852 CNOTs on 23 qubits). On IBM's ibm_kingston, reading only the attention overlaps, the device gave the model's answers on the two shortest test pairs, also when the one word that decides one of them was deleted; with calibration circuits as deep as the overlaps, each word's evidence with the device's attention row sums followed the exact evidence on one pair (correlation 0.997) and on the other less closely (0.962).
papers.authors: Teerawat Tongloy, Jiraporn Pongsopa, Rangsan Jomtarak

papers.title: Weyl Rescalings: A First Order Approach
papers.abstract: Weyl transformations, --local rescalings in which the metric transforms as $g_{\mu\nu}(x)\longrightarrow \Omega^2(x)\, g_{\mu \nu}(x)$--, are expected to be a symmetry of nature at extremely high energy, that should be (spontaneously) broken at low energy. In Cartan's first order formulation of gravity this translates into the condition that the local frames (vielbein) scale as $e^a(x) \longrightarrow \Omega(x) e^a(x)$. In this construction, the Lorentz connection one-form fields $\omega^a{}_b$ are independent from $e^a$, and since Lorentz transformations and dilatations commute, $\omega$ and $R(\omega)$ must be Weyl invariant, while in the second order metric formalism the Ricci tensor undergoes a non-homogeneous transformation. This generates a tension between the two formulations, which should be equivalent in the vanishing torsion limit. Here we show how the puzzle can be resolved taking into account the role of torsion. This also sheds some light on the conformal coupling of matter fields to gravity.
papers.authors: L. Andrianopoli, J. Zanelli

papers.title: Interaction-driven Weyl superfluids from topologically trivial bands in an optical Raman lattice
papers.abstract: We propose an interaction-driven route to Weyl superfluidity from topologically trivial noninteracting bands in a three-dimensional optical Raman lattice. The scheme builds on a pairing mechanism arising from the interplay between a large Zeeman splitting and an attractive Hubbard interaction. The large Zeeman splitting renders the noninteracting bands topologically trivial and suppresses spin-flip hopping. These otherwise off-resonant spin-flip processes are resonantly restored when the attractive Hubbard interaction compensates the energy mismatch, generating occupation-dependent spin-orbit coupling that coherently couples neighboring spin-down fermion pairs to onsite doublons. Combining this density-dependent in-plane spin-orbit coupling with density-dependent spin-conserving interlayer tunneling extends the pairing mechanism to three dimensions. A self-consistent mean-field treatment of the microscopic model yields Weyl superfluids with two, four, or eight nodes, together with fully gapped weak topological superfluids. Tuning the interaction strength and particle filling drives transitions between these phases and controls the number of Weyl nodes. We further propose an experimental implementation with ultracold ${}^{40}\mathrm{K}$ atoms. Our results provide a route to Weyl superfluidity enabled by interaction-assisted spin-orbit coupling, without requiring nontrivial single-particle band topology.
papers.authors: Yong-Huan Wang, Xin-Chi Zhou

papers.title: Dynamical-mean-field cluster-correlation expansion of NV$^-$ spin-echo decoherence in a realistic substitutional-nitrogen bath
papers.abstract: The Hahn-echo time $T_2$ of nitrogen-vacancy (NV$^-$) ensembles in nitrogen-rich diamond follows the empirical relation $T_2\cdot$[N] = 160 $\mu$s ppm, and this relation does not depend on the magnetic field between 2 and 30 mT. Cluster-correlation-expansion (CCE) calculations solve the spin dynamics exactly within small groups of spins. When they treat the Overhauser field of the surrounding P1 centres, that is, the field that these electron spins produce, as frozen, they overestimate $T_2$ at high field by up to a factor of two. This excess was recently attributed to additional dark defects. We show that the excess comes mostly from the frozen field. In our model the P1 centres outside each cluster flip-flop in pairs: two centres exchange their spin states and conserve their total $S_z$. Kinetic Monte Carlo generates these events at golden-rule rates, which follow from the dipolar Hamiltonian without adjustable parameters, and each cluster evolves in the resulting time-dependent field. This dynamical mean field lies between the static-mean-field and mean-field-free limits. For a $^{14}$N P1 bath it reduces $T_2\cdot$[N] at 30 mT from 264 $\pm$ 16 to 188 $\pm$ 12 $\mu$s ppm and gives 167 $\pm$ 11 $\mu$s ppm at 10 mT, 1.7 and 0.4 standard deviations from experiment, with no dark spins. When each centre jumps independently, $T_2\cdot$[N] is 147 $\pm$ 9 $\mu$s ppm at 30 mT; the correlation of the flip-flop partners thus lengthens $T_2$ by 20-30 percent at high field. The Overhauser field is neither frozen nor averaged out by fast motion: 68-83 percent of its autocorrelation survives 200 $\mu$s. At 2.5 mT, where the P1 electron and nucleus hybridise, $T_2$ stays below experiment for any choice of rates. Part of the field dependence therefore remains: $T_2$ rises by a factor 1.69 $\pm$ 0.07 instead of 2.15 $\pm$ 0.08 from 2.5 to 30 mT.
papers.authors: Chikara Shinei

papers.title: Two-scale estimates for limit-periodic Schr\"odinger operators
papers.abstract: We prove strong ballistic transport for one-dimensional continuum Schr\"odinger operators by comparing the spectral geometry at two consecutive periods. Enlarging a period decomposes each fiber into the eigenspaces of translation by the smaller cell. Away from the larger-period symmetry momenta, a simple ordered band remains in one translation sector and agrees with one translated smaller-period band. This permits us to combine large-period ordering and non-overlap with a smaller-period derivative bound. We obtain lower bounds for folded band widths and confine all near-collisions to a common neighborhood of the symmetry momenta, with the exponential cost at the smaller period. For nested periods $p_n$ with $p_{n+1}/p_n\in\mathbb{N}$ and $p_{n+1}\ge2p_n$, approximation errors $o(p_{n+1}^{-2}e^{-\eta p_n})$, where $\eta>7\sqrt{2R}$ and $\|V\|_\infty\le R$, give a nonzero strong asymptotic velocity on a weighted $H^2$ class containing the Schwartz space. Every position moment of order $0<r\le4$ has two-sided ballistic growth. A period-uniform form estimate, ordered-gap summation, and a linear dynamical comparison complete the argument. No upper bound on successive period ratios is assumed, and the sufficient approximation exponents are not claimed to be optimal.
papers.authors: Moises Gomez Solis

papers.title: Lorentzian entropy, subgaussian matrix concentration, and sharp functional inequalities for all matroids
papers.abstract: We prove complete entropy contraction for homogeneous Lorentzian laws and derive subgaussian matrix concentration and sharp functional inequalities for every matroid. Uniform retention of $\ell$ out of $r$ particles contracts matrix entropy by the optimal universal factor $\ell/r$, in every finite matrix dimension and positive field, including repeated labels. The matrix Laplace comparison retains matrix variance and arbitrary Hermitian offsets. It gives subgaussian bounds for arbitrary Hermitian observables with bounded exchange differences, and Chernoff and Bernstein bounds for basis sums. Every unit-edge matroid basis graph satisfies the cube's small-set and Gross inequalities, with equality classified and optimal universal complete entropy-decay rate four. Its spectrum lies in $\{0,2\}\cup[3,\infty)$, with binary direct-factor contrasts spanning the eigenspace at two. We classify extremal down-up eigenfunctions, resolving Alaniz Pintos's degree-one conjecture and the equality problem for the Feder--Mihail walk. For degree at least two, every matrix entropy extremizer extends uniquely from its two-particle marginal. Equality depends only on the normalized pair law, with noncommutativity confined to mutually exclusive labels. We classify power-entropy extremizers for $1<p<2$ and give a fourth-order criterion for affine equality. Retained-level Gibbs reconstruction has sharp dimension-independent stability. For multiaffine laws whose generating polynomial and complement are Lorentzian, we determine the exact simultaneous all-field quantum marginal and matrix H\"older regions and classify the sharp half-marginal fields. Connected sharp laws are determinantal through rank three; stable nondeterminantal examples exist in every higher rank.
papers.authors: Eren Ercan

papers.title: Two-Fluid Radial Stability of Dark-Matter-Admixed Compact Objects: Dark Compact Planets, Dark White Dwarfs, Dark Neutron Stars, and Dark Oysters
papers.abstract: We investigate the equilibrium structure and stability against radial oscillations of a variety of two-fluid compact objects containing ordinary baryonic matter admixed with cold dark matter coupled through the background spacetime. For the ordinary fluid, we employ a QCD equation of state compatible with chiral effective field theory at nuclear densities (supplemented by the BPS and Negele-Vautherin models at extremely low densities) and with perturbative QCD in the high-density regime while also satisfying also current astrophysical data. For the dark fluid, we assume self-interacting fermionic matter with particle masses of $m_f=$ 2, 5, 10, and 100 GeV and two self-interaction strengths of $y=0.1$ and $10^3$. By scanning a large range of central pressures for both fluids, we identify the presence of dark compact planets, dark white dwarfs, dark neutron stars and the so-called dark oysters. Importantly, these objects are not only in two-fluid hydrostatic equilibrium, but they are also stable against two-fluid radial oscillations. We find that the relative representation of each class in the radially stable sample is strongly sensitive to the combinations of $m_f$ and $y$, with some combinations entirely suppressing some of these object classes within the sampled domain while favoring others. In addition to these classes, strong self-repulsion supports stable, dark-matter-dominated branches with compact ordinary-matter cores and extended dark halos, approaching the self-interacting fermion-star limit. Finally, we calculate the gravitational redshift at the ordinary-matter surface, $z_{\rm OM}$, including the contribution of extended dark-matter halos for which we found radially stable configurations with $z_{\rm OM}>2$.
papers.authors: Jos\'e C. Jim\'enez, Oscar Pastor, Laura Tolos

papers.title: Toric codes all the way down: decoupling translation-invariant topological CSS codes in higher dimensions
papers.abstract: Topological Calderbank-Shor-Steane (CSS) codes in more than two spatial dimensions offer features useful for fault-tolerant quantum computation, such as transversal non-Clifford gates and single-shot decoding, but a systematic understanding of them is still lacking. One approach is to decouple a code: map it to a stack of higher-form toric codes by a finite-depth local CSS-preserving Clifford circuit, possibly after adding ancillas. For translation-invariant $p$-ary CSS codes, where $p$ is prime ($p=2$ for qubits), we require the circuit to commute with the translations of a superlattice. In two dimensions, such a decoupling exists once these translations act trivially on every anyon type. In higher dimensions, excitations are sorted by their dimension into superselection layers, which can remain glued together even when translations act trivially on each layer. We show that this gluing is the only remaining obstruction: a code can be decoupled on a superlattice exactly when, after coarse-graining to it, translations act trivially on every layer and the gluing vanishes. Moreover, for a code with finitely many excitation types in each layer and $m$ nonzero layers, once translations act trivially on every layer, further coarse-graining by a factor of $p^{m-1}$ in every direction removes the aforementioned gluing. Physically, the same criterion determines when the code encodes the maximal number of logical qudits on a finite torus. Finally, we give an explicit algorithm that constructs the decoupling as a circuit of SUM (qudit CNOT) and SWAP gates.
papers.authors: Mingxin He, Yifei Wang, Hao Song, Yingfei Gu

papers.title: Distributed Inner-Product Estimation for Continuous-Variable Quantum States
papers.abstract: Distributed inner-product estimation (DIPE) is a fundamental task in quantum information, aiming to estimate the inner product between two unknown quantum states prepared on separate quantum platforms. In multimode continuous-variable (CV) systems, the infinite-dimensional Hilbert space poses additional challenges. In this work, we propose a protocol for CV-DIPE that requires the two platforms to share a common phase reference and perform local homodyne measurements at the same randomly sampled phase settings, followed by classical post-processing of the measurement data. We derive explicit upper bounds on the sample complexity of this protocol. These bounds depend on the available physical prior information. Specifically, we provide bounds for two natural cases: finite-energy states and Gaussian states. Through numerical simulations, we demonstrate the theoretical performance of this estimation scheme. Our findings offer a CV-DIPE protocol that relies solely on homodyne measurements and remains applicable even when neither of the two quantum states is fully characterized.
papers.authors: Jun Tang, Congcong Zheng, Yujie Miao, Xutao Yu, Zaichen Zhang

papers.title: Are quantum measurements universal?
papers.abstract: In 2014, with D. Aerts, we showed, in the extended Bloch representation of quantum mechanics, that the Born rule results from a universal average over all the ways the measurement-interaction can be selected, computed by averaging over discretized (cellular) densities and taking a continuum limit. N. Shackel has since criticized this construction, in the context of Bertrand's paradox, for depending on the discretization adopted, for the constancy of its averages, and for the unclear sense in which the average is over 'all' densities. His criticisms prompt the present re-examination. What makes a random way of selecting a measurement 'universal', we argue, is that it privileges no portion of the structure of the available interactions, a property we call indifference and adopt as definitional. We prove that every universal measurement, however constructed, produces exactly the Born probabilities: the universal average is unique, the 2014 construction is one realization among infinitely many, and for cellular measurements the result is exact at every finite resolution, with no limit to be taken, which explains the constancy of the averages. Non-trivial universal measurements exist, but must involve deterministic measurements: Dirichlet processes are universal measurements whose support contains every way of selecting an interaction, whereas one free of deterministic components selects the uniform density, so that for it the Born rule holds with certainty, not merely on average. In sequences of measurements, deterministic components produce deviations from quantum statistics governed by a single parameter, in principle accessible to experiment. The only geometric input is the Euclidean length of the membrane and the orthogonal landing of the point-particle, where Gleason's theorem enters. We indicate the generalization to any number of outcomes and the bearing on Bertrand's paradox.
papers.authors: Massimiliano Sassoli de Bianchi

papers.title: Cosmological constraints on single-field inflation models from ACT/SPT data and observations at sub-Mpc scales
papers.abstract: We investigate single-field inflation models that can produce large curvature perturbations at sub-Mpc scales while remaining consistent with cosmological observations across multiple regimes. We highlight the tension between generating enhanced small-scale perturbations and maintaining agreement with the scalar spectral index $n_s$ measured by ACT and SPT, which disfavors several conventional single-field inflation models. To address this issue, we propose three viable classes of inflationary potentials: bump/dip-modified, step-like, and double-inflection-point. Each can sufficiently amplify primordial perturbations while predicting $n_s$ that lie within the $2\sigma$ range of current observational bounds. In addition, we examine the primordial power spectra predicted by these models and constrain their parameter spaces using cosmological observations at different scales, including CMB, BAO, PBH, PTA, and CMB-distortion. Our results show that some of the models considered can simultaneously satisfy the ACT/SPT constraints and account for the current PTA observations, although doing so while respecting the constraints on the PBH abundance remains challenging.
papers.authors: Qing-Yang Wang, Jing-Zhi Zhou, Fei-Yu Chen, Zhi-Chao Li

papers.title: Corner Regularity and Asymptotics for the Two-Dimensional Radiation Transport Equation
papers.abstract: The regularity of solutions to the two-dimensional radiation transport equation plays a central role in understanding the behavior of scalar flux near geometric corners. In a previous study of Kaper's corner singularity problem, the physical transport kernel was decomposed into its principal inverse-distance singularity and a lower-order remainder, reducing the corner asymptotic analysis to the question of whether the scalar flux possesses sufficient continuity to justify differentiation of the associated singular potential. The required regularity, however, remained unresolved. In this paper, we establish a sharp modulus-of-continuity estimate for the scalar flux generated by the physical transport kernel and prove the estimate $\omega_{\phi}(h)=O\!\left(h\log(D/h)\right)$, which implies Dini continuity. This estimate yields absolute convergence of the fluctuation term arising in the differentiated principal potential and permits a rigorous differentiation formula for transport solutions. Using this regularity framework, we derive the fixed-angle asymptotic behavior of the scalar flux and its first derivatives near a rectangular corner. For every fixed interior ray, the gradient exhibits logarithmic growth, while the scalar flux admits an $r\log(1/r)$ correction with an explicitly identified coefficient determined by the corner values of the flux and source. The analysis shows that a rectangular corner does not generate a singularity stronger than the logarithmic first-derivative singularity already present in smooth-boundary transport theory. Numerical calculations on benchmark problems are consistent with the theoretical predictions. These results provide a rigorous resolution of the regularity issue underlying Kaper's corner singularity problem and establish a mathematical framework for corner asymptotics in two-dimensional radiation transport.
papers.authors: Dean Wang

papers.title: QuantumBilliards.jl: An extensible, user friendly, high-performance Julia library for the large scale computation of spectra and eigenstates of quantum billiards and related problems
papers.abstract: We present QuantumBilliards.jl, an open-source Julia library providing a suite of numerical solvers for the two-dimensional interior Helmholtz eigenproblem with Dirichlet boundary conditions, a paradigmatic model in quantum chaos. The library implements conventional wavenumber-sweep techniques together with several accelerated eigensolvers: the Vergini--Saraceno scaling method, the expanded boundary integral method (EBIM), Beyn's contour-integral method, and the Compact Rational Krylov (CORK) method. It provides a common framework for constructing billiard geometries, exploiting discrete symmetries, computing eigenvalues and eigenstates, and treating smooth, cornered, and multiply connected domains. The library further includes reconstruction of eigenfunctions from boundary normal derivatives and the computation of Poincar\'e--Husimi (PH) phase-space representations. Available at: https://github.com/Quantum-Chaos-Julia/QuantumBilliards.jl.
papers.authors: Matic Orel, \v{C}rt Lozej

papers.title: Timelike Supersymmetric Geometries in Seven-Dimensional Supergravity
papers.abstract: Seven-dimensional supergravity poses a uniquely intricate supersymmetry problem, combining topologically massive higher-form gauge dynamics, distinct Clifford algebra properties, and rich geometric structures. We first establish the complete formulation of the maximal Cartan-gauged theory in terms of the gauge-invariant higher-form flux, including both the bosonic action and supersymmetry variations. This formulation, which also makes the smooth ungauged limit manifest, is achieved by requiring a consistent truncation to the minimal Cartan-gauged theory in the equal-charge limit. We construct the complete bilinear system for a timelike Killing vector, where additional internal orientation of the symplectic-Majorana spinor arises already in the scalar sector, uniquely among pure minimal ungauged theories. In the equal-charge sector, we decouple the algebraic constraints into SU$(3)$-isotypic components, and analyse the differential bilinear relations, determining the permitted dilaton gradient, fluxes, fibration twist and intrinsic torsion of the base. We prove that with gauging and active Cartan flux, the complex scalar bilinear vanishes identically. We also construct a Killing gauge for the higher-form potential compatible with the self-duality condition. We show that with gauging but no active Cartan flux, the Killing vector also acts as a generator of the gauged R-symmetry, and the base structure is enlarged from SU$(3)$ to U$(3)$. We find that BPS-flow solutions realize this setting. With supersymmetry, we isolate a single independent component of the 3-form equation across an exhaustive four-class partition for both theories within this setup. Applied to known and proposed solutions in both theories, this classification exposes unexplored sectors and provides an accessible toolbox for constructing and testing solutions and developing new geometric and holographic applications.
papers.authors: Mich\`ele Levi

papers.title: Low-field dephasing time of an optically polarized NV$^-$ spin bath beyond the P1 limit in diamond: a cluster-correlation-expansion and exact spin-bath study
papers.abstract: Dense ensembles of nitrogen-vacancy (NV$^-$) centres in nitrogen-rich diamond dephase on the electron spins of the substitutional nitrogen (P1) centres. If the paramagnetic nitrogen is instead converted into NV$^-$ centres, the laser that initializes the sensor also pumps the bath into $m_s = 0$, a state with no moment along its own axis. Using cluster-correlation-expansion (CCE) calculations with a dynamical mean field, combined with an exact solver for probe-bath exchange and with no adjustable parameter, this paper asks whether such an optically polarized NV$^-$ bath dephases a sensor more slowly than a P1 bath of the same density. The answer is set by the field. In a field along [111], three quarters of the bath centres lie off the field axis, and the moment of their $m_s = 0$ state along the field grows from 0.04 at 25 G to 0.46 at 300 G and 0.81 at 800 G. At 25 G the polarized bath is therefore nearly silent: at 0.57 ppm the dephasing time $T_2^*$ of a separately addressed $^{15}$NV$^-$ probe is 112 $\mu$s, six times the 18.0 $\mu$s of a P1 bath, and still 2.4 times at 90% polarization; an ensemble measurement gains a factor of two. At 300 G the advantage over P1 shrinks to 1.4, and at 800 G the polarized bath dephases faster than P1. The field dependence of every bath, P1 included, follows the mean moment of its centres along the field. For the Hahn echo, bath relaxation ($T_1$ = 6 ms) caps the gain: a $^{15}$NV$^-$ probe in a polarized bath reaches 1.5 times the P1 value at 25 G and 1.14-1.16 times at 300 and 800 G. Optical polarization of an NV$^-$ bath at low field therefore offers dephasing times beyond the P1 limit of nitrogen-rich diamond.
papers.authors: Chikara Shinei

papers.title: Sharp Quantitative Convergence of Compactly Supported Aggregation-Diffusion
papers.abstract: We establish the quantitative convergence of nonlinear aggregation-diffusion equations in dimension one, with sublinear attraction kernel and degenerate diffusion higher than quadratic. In these models, steady state is known to be the unique, compactly supported, and radial decreasing probability distribution. In this paper, we work with compactly supported densities in dimension one, we prove these solutions converge to the steady state exponentially fast.
papers.authors: Yunhong Deng

papers.title: Stable and causal frames for BDNK hydrodynamics
papers.abstract: We establish the existence of families of linearly stable and causal Bemfica-Disconzi-Noronha-Kovtun (BDNK) frames for arbitrary equation of state and set of physical transport coefficients. By developing a method based on simplification of Routh-Hurwitz criteria and telegrapher factorisation of polynomials, we provide six concrete examples of such families, three of which admit conformal limits, for both neutral and charged fluids. These frames have adjustable characteristic speeds and can serve as a starting point for numerical implementations of relativistic hydrodynamics in various settings. In the process we uncover a map between stable and causal frames in neutral fluids and stable and causal frames in charged fluids. We also develop an AI research protocol that can be used to search for such frames in any hydrodynamic theory.
papers.authors: Jay Armas

papers.title: Probing parity-breaking black-hole geometry with extreme-mass-ratio inspirals
papers.abstract: We investigate the gravitational-wave signatures of equatorial reflection symmetry breaking in extreme-mass-ratio inspirals (EMRIs) around a parity-violating conformal Kerr black hole. For the circular-orbit branch connected to equatorial Kerr orbits, we derive the dynamics through second order in the dimensionless deformation parameter $\varepsilon$ and construct adiabatic inspirals and gravitational-wave signals using a mass-quadrupole prescription. Equatorial reflection maps $\varepsilon$ to $-\varepsilon$, making the polar displacement odd and the orbital frequency and energy even in the deformation. The induced first harmonic has a small direct contribution for the configurations studied, while second-order dynamical corrections accumulate over many cycles to produce appreciable dephasing. We find that rapid black-hole rotation enhances these phase effects and the associated noise-weighted waveform mismatch. For a one-year inspiral of a $10M_\odot$ object into a $10^6M_\odot$ black hole with $a/M=0.9$ and viewing inclination $\iota=2\pi/3$, the fixed-parameter mismatch reaches the comparison benchmark $\mathcal M=0.01$ at approximately $\varepsilon=10^{-3}$, without optimization over time, phase, or Kerr parameters. A single-parameter Fisher analysis also indicates improved local sensitivity to $\varepsilon$ at high spin. These results connect the reflection properties of the circular branch to accumulated source-phase effects and complement tests of propagation birefringence.
papers.authors: Zhen-Bo Wu, Qing Ou, Peng-Cheng Li

papers.title: No-Go Theorem for Phantom Crossing in Scalar-Tensor Gravity with Non-Minimal Derivative Coupling and Soft Scale-Invariance Breaking
papers.abstract: Recent baryon acoustic oscillation measurements from the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI 2024) reveal a preference for dynamical dark energy with an equation of state parameter crossing the phantom divide ($w < -1$) at low redshifts. We investigate whether this phantom crossing can be realized within scale-invariant scalar-tensor theories featuring non-minimal derivative coupling (NMDC) between the scalar field and the Einstein tensor. Employing the effective field theory of dark energy formalism, we systematically derive the ghost-free and gradient stability conditions, and examine their compatibility with the swampland conjectures from quantum gravity. We establish three rigorous no-go theorems demonstrating that: (i)~phantom crossing necessitates $\xi_{\text{eff}} < 0$, directly violating the no-ghost stability requirement $\xi_{\text{eff}} > 0$; (ii)~the swampland de Sitter and distance conjectures independently obstruct phantom crossing; and (iii)~these theoretical obstructions are mutually reinforcing. Our results show that scale-invariant NMDC models cannot account for the DESI preference for $w < -1$, providing robust theoretical guidance for dark energy model building beyond this class.
papers.authors: Reza Baghbani

papers.title: Banded Totally Positive Matrices and Positive Bidiagonal Factorizations: Existence, Stability, and Toeplitz Orthogonality
papers.abstract: A positive bidiagonal factorization of a banded totally positive matrix expresses it as a product of unit lower and upper bidiagonal factors with positive off-diagonal entries and a positive diagonal matrix. In finite dimension such factorizations always exist, with parameter domains defined by polynomial inequalities. In the semi-infinite case, existence is equivalent to convergence of explicit positive series. Every bounded banded totally positive matrix is an operator-norm limit of matrices admitting these factorizations, through perturbations confined to a fixed initial block. Necessary and sufficient criteria characterize analytic dependence of prescribed factors on perturbations. With fixed initial entries, a relative entrywise criterion allows unbounded factors with different growth rates. For uniformly positive bounded factors with variable initial entries, the criterion involves every pair of factors on each triangular side and the signed triangular inverses. The dimensions of the local factorization families are determined. Normalized LDU factors depend analytically at every interior point of the factorization class. For banded totally positive Toeplitz matrices, a stable positive bidiagonal factorization exists if and only if the symbol polynomial has distinct roots. Root formulas give two polynomial vector families with mixed-type multiple orthogonality for a rectangular matrix of positive measures. One factorization simultaneously attains the smallest possible first off-diagonal entries of both normalization matrices. The weighted linear forms are independent of the factorization. Their Chebyshev expansions yield asymptotic zero spacing inside the support and convergence of normalized kernels to the sine kernel after rescaling by the local zero density.
papers.authors: Manuel Ma\~nas

papers.title: Optimal GHZ extraction from MABK violations
papers.abstract: We prove that, for $n\geq3$ parties, the minimum Greenberger-Horne-Zeilinger (GHZ) extractability at normalized Mermin-Ardehali-Belinskii-Klyshko (MABK) score $t\in[0,1]$ is $(1+t)/2$ over all states and binary measurements, allowing arbitrary local dimensions. The extractability $\Xi_n(\rho)$ of a state $\rho$ is the supremum of squared GHZ overlap over local channels. The score $t$ scales linearly from zero at the biseparable bound to one at the quantum maximum. This recovers the three- to five-party bounds and proves the conjecture of Cao et al. for $n\geq6$. We determine the exact qubit minimum, strictly higher for $0<t<1$. We construct a mixture on one qutrit and $n-1$ qubits attaining the bound with fixed measurements and score-dependent weights. We prove that at interior scores it has the smallest product of local ranks among attaining states, $3\cdot2^{n-1}$, and for $n\geq4$ is unique at that product up to local isometries and party permutations. With one qutrit, $n-1$ qubits and arbitrary binary measurements, set $\varepsilon:=\Xi_n(\rho)-(1+t)/2$. For $n\geq4$, $t$ bounded away from zero and small $\varepsilon$, we prove that the state's trace-norm distance to the mixture at score $t$, up to local unitaries, is $O(\sqrt{\varepsilon})$, uniformly in $n$ with optimal exponent. For $n=3$ we bound this distance explicitly above $t_0\approx0.69333$. For $n\geq3$ and $t>0$, we bound this distance from the Bell score and the expectations of five calibrated binary qutrit measurements, given the local dimensions and a known two-dimensional qutrit subspace invariant under both qutrit Bell observables.
papers.authors: Avraham Kreindel (Yohananov), Aryeh Lev Zabokritskiy (Yohananov)

papers.title: Mirror symmetry for gCICY threefolds (I): a $[3,-1]$ block and a non-Gorenstein toric phase
papers.abstract: We construct and analyze a mirror family for the generalized complete intersection Calabi-Yau threefold $X_+=[\mathbb{P}^1\,|\,3\ {-1};\ \mathbb{P}^4\,|\,2\ 3]$, with $(h^{1,1},h^{2,1})=(2,46)$. We introduce auxiliary variables to obtain a toric GIT presentation with two chambers. The first gives $X_+$, while the second gives a Calabi-Yau threefold $X_-$ related to $X_+$ by a flop of 16 disjoint $(-1,-1)$-curves. The threefold $X_-$ is a nef complete intersection in a non-Gorenstein toric $\mathbb{Q}$-Fano eightfold. Then the Hori-Vafa equations give a 2-parameter Laurent family, and we construct a smooth projective crepant model $Y$ of its general member with mirrored Hodge numbers. The rank-6 Picard-Fuchs system of $Y$ has two maximally unipotent boundary points, whose indicial algebras are isomorphic to the even cohomology rings $H^{\mathrm{even}}(X_+,\mathbb{C})$ and $H^{\mathrm{even}}(X_-,\mathbb{C})$. We also show that the predicted genus-zero BPS numbers of the first two vertical degrees agree with direct counts of lines and conics on the genus-one fibration $X_-\to\mathbb{P}^2$.
papers.authors: Atsushi Kanazawa

papers.title: Parallel and Distributed Fermionic Simulation via Dynamic Encoding
papers.abstract: We demonstrate a simple and efficient method to parallelize and distribute Trotterized Hamiltonian simulation of fermionic systems across multiple QPUs. Using combinatorial covering designs to define a fixed set of fermion-qubit encodings, independent of system size, we demonstrate communication cost scaling as $\mathcal{O}(M q^3 r)$ for a system of $M$ fermionic modes and Trotter number $r$. This improves on the static encoding bound for $q$ QPUs, $\mathcal{O}(M^4 q r)$. In terms of QPU register size $R$, at most $R^{1/3}$ QPUs are able to parallelize at most $R^{4/3}$ fermionic modes. We compare this approach to dynamic encoding using a randomized method, Pauli-weight based optimization and hypergraph partitioning. Applying these to the Hamiltonians of a range of molecular systems split across two and three QPUs, we find the combinatorial covering approach results in significantly reduced communication cost.
papers.authors: Michael Williams de la Bastida, Peter V. Coveney

papers.title: Theoretical study of nitrogen-vacancy spin coherence enhanced by vacancy aggregation in diamond using cluster-correlation expansion
papers.abstract: Annealing a semiconductor makes its vacancies mobile; they aggregate into multi-vacancy complexes that often carry spin. Such centres are a magnetic-noise source for any spin qubit among them, in silicon and silicon carbide as well as in diamond, and they are accordingly blamed for the decoherence of negatively charged nitrogen-vacancy (NV$^-$) centres in irradiated and implanted diamond, with two coherence records credited to removing them. Cluster-correlation-expansion simulations in which the spins outside each cluster keep exchanging spin projections in pairs reproduce the measured Hahn-echo coherence time of NV$^-$ centres in a substitutional-nitrogen bath to within 12%, inside the statistical uncertainty. Driven by published electron-paramagnetic-resonance parameters, the same calculation inverts the attribution. At a fixed paramagnetic spin density a multi-vacancy bath gives a Hahn-echo coherence time 3.0-6.1 times longer than a bath of isolated negative vacancies at 1 ppm, and 2.2-6.5 times longer from 0.01 to 10 ppm. A bath dephases the qubit because its spins exchange spin projections with one another, and two can exchange only if their transition frequencies match. A fine-structure splitting shifts those frequencies. Were every defect on the same crystallographic site, all would shift alike and still match, and the splitting would gain little, a factor 1.2. Real defects occupy symmetry-equivalent sites pointing in different directions, so neighbours land at different frequencies and stop exchanging: a factor 2.3. What governs the coherence time is therefore the fraction of bath pairs sharing a transition frequency, not the size of the zero-field splitting. Vacancy aggregation extends NV$^-$ spin coherence rather than shortening it.
papers.authors: Chikara Shinei

papers.title: Bernoulli flow for Erd\H{o}s-R\'enyi graphs
papers.abstract: We study the eigenvalues and eigenvectors of the adjacency matrix $A$ of the Erd\H{o}s-R\'enyi graph $\mathbb G(N,p)$ in the regime $Np \gg (\log N)^2$. We establish optimal isotropic delocalization for the bulk eigenvectors $\boldsymbol u$, meaning that $\langle \boldsymbol v, \boldsymbol u\rangle^2 \leq \frac{C \log N}{N}$ with very high probability for any deterministic normalized $\boldsymbol v$. In addition, we prove local spectral universality in the bulk by showing that the local spectral statistics coincide with those of the GOE. The main tool of our proof is a local law for the resolvent of $A$, down to optimal spectral scales and with optimal error bounds. Its proof relies on a new approach to local laws that we call the Bernoulli flow. It is a characteristic flow method in which the usual Brownian process is replaced by a Bernoulli process, where each edge of the graph forms an independent Markov process that jumps at unit rate from closed to open. The spectral parameter flows according to a suitably constructed matrix-valued Bernoulli characteristic flow.
papers.authors: Joscha Henheik, Antti Knowles

papers.title: Asymmetric quantum error correction efficiently tackles application-specific noise effects
papers.abstract: Noise is a major challenge for current quantum computers. It can be broadly categorized into bit-flip and phase-flip errors. These two types do not necessarily affect the executed algorithm, thus also the application, in the same way. We illustrate this general effect for the example of the quantum approximate optimization algorithm (QAOA) applied to a small instance of the flight-gate assignment (FGA) problem. We compare bit-flip and phase-flip Pauli noise under both layer-level and gate-level noise models, using two circuit decompositions of the same ideal QAOA unitary: a CNOT-based decomposition and a native-RZZ decomposition. For the six-qubit FGA instance considered here, bit-flip noise produces a larger degradation in the optimized QAOA performance across the investigated circuit depths and noise models. The asymmetry is most pronounced in the layer-level and native-RZZ simulations. We explain this behavior through the commutation and propagation properties of the errors and their effects on the final computational-basis measurements. Since these mechanisms are not specific to the considered FGA instance, we expect similar noise asymmetries to arise in other Ising-based QAOA applications, although this remains to be investigated. We then exploit these insights to tackle noise particularly efficiently using asymmetric error-correcting codes. As an illustration, we use the quantum parity code (QPC), a generalization of the 9-qubit Shor code, and show that a smaller asymmetric code can achieve nearly the same improvement as a larger symmetric choice. This suggests that allocating error-correction resources according to algorithmic noise sensitivity, rather than physical error rates alone, can be beneficial even when the physical noise is symmetric. Finally, we discuss how information about the noise obtained through calibration can be exploited in our approach.
papers.authors: Abhishek Yadav, Peter K. Schuhmacher, Michael Epping

papers.title: Implementation of a five-wave approximate Riemann solver for general relativistic magnetohydrodynamics in AthenaK
papers.abstract: We present an implementation of an HLLD approximate Riemann solver for the AthenaK astrophysics code with support for full general relativistic magnetohydrodynamics via a tetrad frame transformation. Our implementation uses an initial guess for the HLLD iterative solve which eliminates the need for an additional conserved-to-primitive inversion, which greatly accelerates performance without affecting accuracy. Additionally, by coupling the method with a first-order flux correction, we are able to use the method reliably even when the magnetization exceeds $10^4$, which we achieve in a SANE accretion disk. Our SANE disk shows that HLLD leads to a more strongly magnetized funnel and more accurate horizon fluxes when compared with HLLE. We further apply the new HLLD implementation to an equal-mass binary neutron star merger. For our long-lived remnant, HLLD enhances the magnetic shear stresses in the outer layers and leads to weaker differential rotation. However, due to weaker gravitational wave emissions in the post-merger phase, the remnant is consistently less compact while producing more dynamical ejecta and a more massive disk. The cost of this new solver is relatively modest thanks to the improved initial guess: our accretion disk tests are only ${\sim}10-25\%$ slower than HLLE, and for our binary neutron star runs with a microphysical equation of state, we find that HLLD is only ${\sim}3\%$ slower than HLLE across all runs.
papers.authors: Jacob Fields, George N. Wong, James M. Stone

papers.title: On the growth of operator entanglement in brickwork circuits with Yang--Baxter gates
papers.abstract: We study the operator entanglement of local operators in one-dimensional brickwork circuits whose two-site gate satisfies the braid relation; throughout this work, we call such a gate a Yang--Baxter gate. We establish upper bounds for several structured, overlapping classes of Yang--Baxter gates. We show that the operator Schmidt rank remains uniformly bounded in time for all qubit Yang--Baxter gates and, in arbitrary local dimension, for permutation gates obtained from non-degenerate Yang--Baxter maps. We also show that it grows at most polynomially for involutive dual-unitary Yang--Baxter gates and for arbitrary phase dressings of permutation gates obtained from non-degenerate Yang--Baxter maps. These results imply, respectively, constant and logarithmic upper bounds on the operator entanglement. Conversely, we construct a seven-state involutive Yang--Baxter gate without dual unitarity and a one-site operator whose exact operator Schmidt rank grows exponentially, although the corresponding operator entropies remain undetermined. Entanglement growth in the general Yang--Baxter case remains open. All proofs and selected examples were constructed by ChatGPT.
papers.authors: Bal\'azs Pozsgay

papers.title: Entanglement and magic transitions in an all-to-all non-Hermitian spin model
papers.abstract: The long-time state of a non-Hermitian system is determined by the eigenvalue with the largest imaginary part. In interacting many-body systems this eigenvalue usually cannot be tracked analytically, and the character of the state it selects is unknown. We construct a non-Hermitian spin ensemble of $L$ spins with exactly $k$-local all-to-all interactions, in which this dominant eigenvalue can be tracked analytically from the clean limit into the disordered regime. Disorder produces a competition between an isolated spectral outlier and the edge of a many-body spectral bulk. We study three cases: purely anti-Hermitian disorder, purely Hermitian disorder, and mixed disorder of equal strength. For purely anti-Hermitian and mixed disorder, we show that when the bulk overtakes the outlier in imaginary part, the dominant eigenstate switches from an outlier state with low entanglement and magic (nonstabilizerness) to a bulk state with substantially larger entanglement and magic, with both changing at the same threshold. For $k \gg \sqrt{L}$ the bulk has a sharp spectral edge and the transition thresholds follow in closed form, while for $k \ll \sqrt{L}$ spectral tails broaden the transition into a crossover. Purely Hermitian disorder provides a contrasting case with no outlier-to-bulk switching. Finally, we map the non-Hermitian evolution exactly onto postselected trajectories of a monitored quantum system, connecting this spectral mechanism to measurement-induced transitions.
papers.authors: Sasanka Dowarah, Michael Kolodrubetz

papers.title: Divergence between Maximum-Probability and Maximum-Likelihood Decoding in the Low-Noise Limit of Quantum Error Correction
papers.abstract: In the asymptotic low-noise limit of quantum error correction, two optimal decoding rules can disagree. Maximum-probability (MP) decoding selects the most probable microscopic error, whereas degenerate maximum-likelihood (MLD) decoding selects the logical sector with the largest total probability. Under code-capacity Pauli noise, we determine the first physical error weight $m$ at which the MP and MLD logical winner sets become provably disjoint, even under optimal MP tie resolution. As the physical error rate tends to zero, MLD retains a residual zero-temperature degeneracy from the multiplicity of minimum-weight errors sharing a syndrome and logical label, which can outweigh the single most probable error. Code distance imposes the universal bound $m\geq h=\lceil d/2\rceil$; the rigidity depth $r$, defined by $m=h+r$, counts the additional error-weight shells above $h$ on which MP and MLD remain equivalent. We certify a three-level hierarchy: $r=0$ for planar surface codes and two recursively concatenated families, $r=1$ for odd-distance square toric codes and the Gross $[[144,12,12]]$ quantum low-density-parity-check code, and $r=2$ for a separable family with hypergraph product and bivariate bicycle descriptions. The onset weight fixes the leading failure-rate gap between best-tie MP and MLD, proportional to the $m$th power of the physical noise strength, providing an exact subthreshold benchmark for the advantage of degeneracy-aware decoding over the computationally cheaper nondegenerate rule.
papers.authors: Yixin Zhao, Fei Yan

papers.title: Long-term 3+1 simulations of primordial black hole formation during radiation domination
papers.abstract: We develop an efficient three-dimensional numerical-relativity framework for primordial black-hole (PBH) formation from superhorizon curvature perturbations in a radiation-dominated Universe. We implement flux-conservative relativistic hydrodynamics in the adaptive-mesh-refinement code GRChombo and introduce a cosmologically scaled Gamma-driver that allows the cosmic-time step to grow in proportion to the scale factor. For a representative long-term simulation, the scaled driver preserves the apparent-horizon mass evolution and constraint behavior while reducing the number of coarse-level advances by a factor of approximately $94$ relative to the standard driver. We also construct a conformal-time version of the moving-puncture gauge as a consistency check. Applying the framework to a spherical Gaussian curvature profile, we find a collapse threshold $\mu_c \simeq 0.7958$ and approximate critical mass scaling, consistent with previous spherically symmetric results. We further fit the late-time PBH mass growth to the Zel'dovich--Novikov accretion law, demonstrating that the code can follow both near-critical collapse and long-term post-formation evolution in three dimensions. The framework provides a foundation for future studies of PBH formation beyond spherical symmetry.
papers.authors: Zhuan Ning, Rong-Gen Cai, Shao-Jiang Wang, Chul-Moon Yoo

papers.title: Entanglement-assisted quantum locally recoverable codes: bounds and constructions with availability
papers.abstract: In this work, we define entanglement-assisted quantum locally recoverable codes with availability, in which any set of up to $\delta-1$ erased qudits can be recovered from any one of $t$ local recovery sets, each of size at most $r+\delta-1$, with the recovery sets intersecting exactly in the erased coordinates, where $r$ is a (small) positive integer.
